the interaction between GO with ss nucleic acids.
the desorption of ssDNA or RNA from GO surface by disrupting hydrogen bonds between the ssDNA or RNA and GO surface.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hydrogen bonds are important in the interaction between single-stranded nucleotides and GO.
GO is an effective adsorbent for single-stranded DNA and RNA and that the interaction between GO with single-stranded DNA or RNA is primarily through hydrogen bonding.
the hydrogen bonds between the hexagonal cells on GO and single-strands of nucleic acids are disrupted by urea, resulting in the desorption of single-strands of the nucleic acids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

GO can be used to extract ssDNA and RNA from cells and that the bound ssDNA/RNA can be readily eluted from GO with the aid of urea, which is a simple and effective method to extract nucleic acid from cells and other samples.
GO can interact with ssDNA or RNA through pi-stacking and hydrogen bonding.

single-stranded nucleobases can be adsorbed onto GO surface through pi-stacking and hydrogen bonding, and the hydrogen bonds can be disrupted with urea, leading to the desorption of ssDNA and RNA from the GO surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adsorption of ss nucleic acids on GO can be easily reversed by disrupting hydrogen bonding between the hexagonal cells and the nucleobases.
GO can be used to extract single-stranded nucleics and the interaction between nucleic acids and GO can be controlled by disrupting hydrogen bonding.
the hydrogen bonds between the single-stranded nucleobases and GO are easily disrupted with a small amount of urea, and the single-stranded regions of the DNA or RNA can be easily desorbed.
